# DC segmenting Markdown→wiki renderer (pure capability)

## Problem
Jira Data Center stores descriptions as lossy wiki markup. WikiTextCodec is currently identity, so raw Markdown appears as literal source. Whole-body pandoc conversion is unsafe for punctuation-dense prose: arrows, regular expressions, HTML-dense text, plus ASCII tables can be misparsed or eroded. The corpus experiment found that a segmenting renderer can enrich about 68% of bodies / 78% of characters while preserving dangerous units.

This story adds only a pure renderer module. It does not change WikiTextCodec, OutboundFieldMapper, the DC CREATE path, or any live send site. Wiring is intentionally deferred to disparaged-parodistic-shrew, where rendering lands together with echo suppression, rollback, plus second-pass convergence.

## Existing contracts
- RichTextCodec and WikiTextCodec live in adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py.
- WikiTextCodec fit_outbound, normalize_outbound, to_wire, plus decode_inbound remain identity in this story.
- The codec law normalize_outbound(t) == decode_inbound(to_wire(t)) remains green unchanged.
- backend.py normalize_rich_text is the shared inbound decoder used by agentic-dev-platform; it remains unchanged.
- ADR 0035 forbids jira_family from importing Cloud adapter modules.

## Implementation
Add adapters/jira_family/wiki_render.py with:

    render_markdown_to_wiki(markdown: str) -> str

Split the body into ordered blocks plus list items. Classify each unit before rendering. Send structurally safe headings, lists, fenced code, quotes, plus safe paragraphs through pandoc using -f commonmark -t jira --wrap=none. Pass regex-heavy or HTML-dense units through unchanged.

Apply prose-arrow substitutions (->, <-, <->, => to their Unicode forms) to Markdown before pandoc. Skip fenced code plus inline code, so code such as obj->method() remains byte-identical.

Detect ASCII pipe tables before pandoc. Wrap each table verbatim in {noformat} so repeated processing cannot shorten table separator rows. Preserve block order exactly when reassembling.

Pin pypandoc-binary rather than system pypandoc so CI plus supported installs receive the binary from the wheel. Probe availability once. If the binary is unavailable or conversion raises, return the original Markdown unchanged plus log the fallback once. Timeout/process hardening plus GPL/SBOM work belong to ashy-waterlog-hamadryas.

## Hermetic corpus
Commit the sanitized fixture under tests/fixtures/dc_wiki_corpus/. It is produced from the established ticket corpus experiment, never fetched at test time. It includes the 179 known code-arrow bodies plus 70 table-erosion bodies, including the 9115→9110 ratchet example.

## Tests
Happy path: a heading, checklist, plus fenced code render through render_markdown_to_wiki into h1., wiki bullets, plus {code} in original order.

Held-out edges:
- A mixed body wraps an ASCII table in {noformat}, changes a prose arrow, preserves an inline-code arrow, plus leaves regex/HTML-dense blocks unchanged.
- All 179 code-arrow fixtures retain code arrows while prose arrows convert.
- All 70 erosion fixtures keep identical table bytes through five renderer passes.
- A missing pandoc returns the exact input plus emits only one fallback log.
- The corpus coverage calculation reaches the recorded enrichment floor without prose corruption.

Existing WikiTextCodec identity and codec-law tests must remain unmodified plus green. No contention test is required: this leaf is a pure function plus a process boundary with no store read/write composition, retry state, cache, or snapshot.

## Surface parity census
- CLI command: out of scope; the pure renderer has no command surface.
- MCP/API tool: out of scope; no tool exposes this internal capability directly.
- Library facade: out of scope; no public rebar import is added.
- Automated callers: out of scope in this leaf; the cutover story owns production callers.
- Dual direction: out of scope by design; DC rendering is one-way while synchronization safety belongs to the cutover story.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] render_markdown_to_wiki renders structurally safe units while preserving their original order; verified by the happy-path unit test.
- [ ] Dangerous regex-heavy units pass through byte-identically; verified by the mixed-body edge test.
- [ ] HTML-dense units pass through byte-identically; verified by the mixed-body edge test.
- [ ] Prose-arrow substitution runs before pandoc; verified by a prose -> becoming →.
- [ ] Code arrows remain unchanged in all 179 fixture bodies.
- [ ] Every ASCII table is wrapped in {noformat}.
- [ ] All 70 erosion fixtures retain table bytes over five passes, including the known ratchet body.
- [ ] pypandoc-binary is pinned in project metadata.
- [ ] Missing pandoc returns the exact input plus logs the fallback once.
- [ ] The vendored corpus meets the recorded enrichment floor with zero detected prose corruption.
- [ ] WikiTextCodec plus the live DC send sites remain unchanged, proven by the existing identity and codec-law tests.
